hero_kpi_rationale: EPAM Systems reaches $5.46 billion in revenue in 2025 with 15.4% growth, driven by digital engineering, cloud, and AI services, bolstered by the strategic acquisitions of NEORIS and First Derivative.
company_description: EPAM Systems, Inc. provides digital platform engineering and software development services worldwide. The company offers engineering services, including requirements analysis and platform selection, customization, cross-platform migration, implementation, and integration; cloud services for creating a roadmap to set and refine IT and business goals while identifying new and emerging opportunities leveraging cloud technologies; data, analytics and artificial intelligence; customer experience; marketing; and cybersecurity. It also offers operation solutions comprising integrated engineering practices and smart automation services. In addition, the company offers software product and platform development services, which comprise product research, customer experience design and prototyping, program management, component design and integration, full lifecycle software testing, product deployment and end-user customization, performance tuning, product support and maintenance, managed services, as well as cross-platform migration and modernizing legacy platforms. kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated from digital transformation and software engineering services.
kpis.description: Revenue reaches $5.46 billion in 2025, growing 15.4%, with 9.2% contribution from the acquisitions of NEORIS and First Derivative in Q4 2024.
kpis.signal: Robust growth driven by AI, cloud, and acquisitions

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue remaining after deducting cost of services, excluding depreciation.
kpis.description: Gross margin stands at 28.8% in 2025 (100% - 71.2% cost of revenue ratio), up 1.9 points from 26.9% in 2024, reflecting improved operational efficiency.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating income divided by total revenue, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Operating margin declines to 9.5% in 2025 from 11.5% in 2024, likely due to post-acquisition integration costs and strategic investments in AI and cloud.

kpis.name: R&D Investment (% of Revenue)
kpis.explanation: Spending related to innovation and development of new technology offerings, as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: R&D expenses (including amortization) represent 1.8% of revenue in 2025, up from 1.4% in 2024, supported by EPAM AI/RUN and DIALX Lab initiatives.
kpis.signal: Accelerated investments in AI and proprietary platforms

kpis.name: Total Headcount (in thousands)
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees worldwide at the end of the period.
kpis.description: EPAM had approximately 65,000 employees at the end of 2025, a strong 15% increase driven by the acquisitions of NEORIS and First Derivative in Q4 2024.
kpis.signal: Rapid workforce growth supported by strategic acquisitions

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €4.9 Bn in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of €0.14 Bn in the latest year

kpis.name: Cash & Equivalents
kpis.description: Cash & equivalents extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Cash & equivalents of €1.3 Bn in the latest year

kpis.name: Financial Services Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from clients in the financial services sector, EPAM's largest vertical.
kpis.description: Financial Services represent 24.1% of total revenue with $1.32 billion in 2025, growing 28.6% from $1.02 billion in 2024, remaining the largest vertical.
kpis.signal: Strong growth driven by digital transformation and AI in financial institutions

kpis.name: Americas Revenue (Geographic)
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from clients based in North, Central, and South America.
kpis.description: The Americas represent 58.7% of total revenue with $3.20 billion in 2025, growing 12.9% from $2.84 billion in 2024, driven by acquisitions and existing demand.
kpis.signal: Solid organic growth in the largest geographic region

risks.title: Uncertain Accounting Estimates
risks.summary: Accounting judgments and estimates, particularly on revenue and business combinations, can significantly impact reported results.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is discussed in the introduction of critical accounting policies, with strong language on estimation uncertainty. It directly affects financial statements and is recurring annually. The Capital category is heavily weighted.

risks.title: Variable Revenue Recognition
risks.summary: Estimating variable revenue amounts (discounts, incentives) requires assumptions that may alter reported revenue.
risks.score_rationale: Positioned early in risk factors, with language emphasizing uncertainty and potential material impact. Explicit mention of using judgment for discounts, credits, and incentives. Recurring risk heightened by contract diversity.

risks.title: Business Combinations and Asset Valuations
risks.summary: Valuation of acquired assets and assumed liabilities in acquisitions relies on uncertain estimates that may have lasting impact on results.
risks.score_rationale: Discussed in detail with strong terms such as 'inherently uncertain' and 'significant impact on future amortization'. A large portion of purchase price allocated to intangible assets. Capital category highly weighted.

risks.title: Valuation of Contingent Consideration
risks.summary: The value of future contingent payments (earn-outs) depends on uncertain forecasts and may lead to significant accounting adjustments.
risks.score_rationale: Mention of complex methods (Monte Carlo) and reliance on financial projections. Changes in assumptions lead to direct accounting adjustments. High placement in text and strong language intensity.

risks.title: Customer Concentration
risks.summary: A significant portion of revenue comes from a small number of clients, exposing the company to declines if contracts end.
risks.score_rationale: Although concentration is decreasing, the top 10 clients still represent 21.6% of revenue. Explicit mention of fluctuations related to account maturity. Language is cautious but not alarming.

risks.title: Evolution of Service Models
risks.summary: The shift toward more complex and integrated services requires new skills and may not be adopted as expected by clients.
risks.score_rationale: The move to integrated solutions (AI, cybersecurity, cloud) is highlighted as a key evolution. This implies risks related to adaptation, skills, and client demand. Forward-looking language with moderate intensity.

ai_positioning.summary: EPAM integrates AI into its services and products, including through strategic acquisitions. The company uses AI to enhance its offerings and potentially its internal operations.
